issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for field 'numberOfLecturers': the UML in problem_statement.md declares numberOfLecturers as int (problem_statement.md line 67), but the solution implementation declares the field as byte (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 9). The solution's constructor parameter and setter also accept byte (solution lines 13 and 50), while the getter returns int. This narrows the stored type compared to the UML and creates an API/type inconsistency that can confuse students and lead to mismatches with tests or expected signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML and problem description by using int for numberOfLecturers throughout. Change the field declaration to 'private int numberOfLecturers;', update the constructor parameter to int, and change the setter signature to accept an int. Keep the getter returning int. This preserves a consistent API and avoids unexpected narrowing of the attribute type.
